title: Indie Games That Became Huge | Terraria, Stardew Valley, Hollow Knight, Among Us, Undertale | Gaming Explained
description: How five indie games grew into global hits, with verified sales milestones for Terraria, Stardew Valley, Hollow Knight and the Among Us surge of 2020.

sections.heading: Small teams, giant hits
sections.script: Not every gaming blockbuster comes from a huge studio with a thousand developers. Some of the biggest hits in the world were made by one person or a handful of friends. In this video we look at indie games that became huge. We cover Terraria, Stardew Valley, Hollow Knight, Among Us and Undertale, and we check their sales and milestones against developer announcements and news reports. Several of these games even appear on the Wikipedia list of best selling video games, right next to titles from the biggest publishers on Earth. A quick note about numbers. Sales are announced at certain moments, so we will tell you the date of each figure. Let us start with a game that has been growing for fifteen years.

sections.heading: Terraria the long running giant
sections.script: Terraria is a two dimensional action adventure sandbox made by Re-Logic and released in twenty eleven. There is no set goal. You create a character, enter a procedurally generated world, dig, build, craft gear and fight bosses to unlock stronger items and new characters who sell goods and offer services. You can play alone or with friends, and it supports mods. In May twenty twenty six, for the fifteenth anniversary, Re-Logic announced that Terraria had sold about seventy million copies. According to reports from GamingOnLinux and Massively Overpowered, that includes around thirty nine point six million on PC, nineteen point seven million on mobile and ten point seven million on consoles.

sections.heading: Terraria and the modding community
sections.script: One reason Terraria lasted so long is its community. Re-Logic revealed that tModLoader, the mod tool for the game, has been downloaded twelve point three million times on Steam. The studio also said that over the past year, the game averaged about four hundred sixty one thousand players per day on PC, with almost half of them playing with tModLoader, and a peak of one point four million players. Re-Logic has promised crossplay is in development and that updates will continue beyond version one point four point six. A physical collector's edition for the fifteenth anniversary has also been announced. Terraria proves that a game with constant updates, mods and a loyal community can keep growing year after year.

sections.heading: Stardew Valley and one developer
sections.script: Stardew Valley is a farm life simulation released in twenty sixteen. You inherit your late grandfather's run down farm, clear land, grow crops, raise animals, fish, mine, fight monsters and build relationships with the townspeople. What makes it special is who made it. Eric Barone, who goes by ConcernedApe, built the game almost entirely by himself over roughly four years, according to PC Gamer. He started with a modest goal of making a Harvest Moon style game to learn the C sharp language, and the project grew from there. The British studio Chucklefish later offered to publish it, which let him finish the job. Sometimes one person with a clear vision is all it takes.

sections.heading: Stardew Valley by the numbers
sections.script: The numbers are impressive. ConcernedApe confirmed in February twenty twenty four that Stardew Valley had sold more than thirty million copies. By December twenty twenty four, the official count had reached forty one million, with about twenty six million of those on PC and seven point nine million on Nintendo Switch. Wikipedia's list of best selling games shows fifty million by early twenty twenty six, although we could not find a developer announcement for that figure, so treat it as an estimate. Barone has also said he will not charge for future updates or paid expansions, and the game later gained multiplayer. Few games have stayed this loved for so long on such a small budget.

sections.heading: Hollow Knight from a game jam
sections.script: Hollow Knight is a Metroidvania released in twenty seventeen by the Australian studio Team Cherry. You play a nameless insect warrior exploring Hallownest, a fallen kingdom full of bosses and hidden lore. Its story starts in Adelaide. Ari Gibson, William Pellen and Rohan Fraser made a game jam entry called Hungry Knight in twenty thirteen, and a later jam with the theme beneath the surface became the first spark of Hollow Knight. The team launched a Kickstarter at the end of twenty fourteen and raised fifty seven thousand one hundred thirty eight Australian dollars, more than twenty thousand above its goal. Team Cherry later said the game has sold around fifteen million copies.

sections.heading: Silksong and a world record wait
sections.script: Fans waited years for the sequel. Hollow Knight Silksong was first announced in twenty nineteen, and in November twenty twenty five Team Cherry confirmed it had sold more than seven million copies in about three months. The studio said that number excludes the large number of players who tried it through Xbox Game Pass. Reports said Silksong passed the sales of every Game of the Year nominee at The Game Awards that year, according to GoSuGamers, and it beat the first count of Clair Obscur Expedition Thirty Three, which had reported five million in October twenty twenty five. These totals are from late twenty twenty five, so they may have grown since. A tiny team from Adelaide became a world famous name.

sections.heading: Among Us the sleeper hit
sections.script: Among Us is an online social deduction game from the American studio Innersloth. It arrived on iOS and Android in June twenty eighteen and on Windows in November that year. Then not much happened. The game only exploded in July and August twenty twenty, after popular Twitch streamers began playing it. According to Know Your Meme, average Twitch viewership went from about four hundred sixty viewers in June to more than fifty three thousand in August, and the game reached one point five million concurrent players on September fifth. CNBC explained how streaming on Twitch and Amazon helped make it a mega hit. The pandemic era also created demand for simple, fun multiplayer games, and Innersloth reportedly canceled a planned sequel to focus on the original.

sections.heading: Undertale and the power of choice
sections.script: Undertale is a role playing game created by the American indie developer Toby Fox and released in September twenty fifteen. You control a child who falls into the Underground, a region full of monsters. Combat includes small bullet hell style attacks to dodge, but you can also choose to spare monsters instead of defeating them. Those choices change the dialogue, the characters and the story. Undertale became a cultural phenomenon, loved for its humour, music and surprises, and it showed that a game made mostly by one creator can touch millions of people. Sales figures for the game vary widely between sources, so we will not quote a number, but its influence on indie design is clear.

sections.heading: What the indie hits have in common
sections.script: Look at the five games together and some patterns appear. They did not need a big marketing budget, because players found them and told their friends. They started with a clear idea, whether that was farming, exploring a dark kingdom, digging underground, finding the impostor or sparing a monster. Many kept growing through free updates, mods or streams. They also arrived on many platforms, from computers to phones and consoles, which meant more players could join. Finally, they were all made by teams who cared deeply about the craft. In an industry known for huge budgets, these hits prove that creativity, patience and community can be just as powerful as money.

sections.heading: Which indie game is your favourite
sections.script: That is our look at indie games that became huge. Terraria passed seventy million sales, Stardew Valley passed forty one million officially, Hollow Knight and its sequel brought Team Cherry worldwide fame, Among Us took over the internet in twenty twenty, and Undertale became a modern classic. Now it is your turn. Which indie game do you think deserves a place on this list, and which one has the most hours in your library? Tell us in the comments. If you like gaming stories about creative small teams, please subscribe to the channel and turn on notifications, because we have many more explainers and histories coming soon.
